responses.text: Oh my, yes! They're a fascinating tribe with a long and, unfortunately, tragic history.
Their original incarnation, much farther out west, was almost completely wiped out by one of those itinerant heroes so common in the post-War years.
Then of course the "New Khans" suffered a similar fate, some say at the hands of the same hero, though of course the dates are all wrong for that.

topics.prompt: Julie Farkas said you might know something about the Great Khans.

responses.text: You look like someone with a question. What can I do for you?
Well, after they migrated to the Mojave, we established relations with them, but that soured when all they wanted was to make drugs.
The NCR eventually took them down quite a bit, but the really fascinating thing about them is the origin of their culture as a whole. You see....
Oh, of course! I'm sorry, I do tend to get wrapped up in my own theories and forget that not everyone finds them as fascinating as I do.
Here, I salvaged this book from an old library. It's a history of a people called the {over-enunciate, like it's unfamiliar} Mongols. I think that's what the Khans built their culture on.
You should read it, it's fascinating stuff.

topics.prompt: Can I get the abridged version?
